item.description: [Open Source Software] Keyword: FOSS — Millions of years after animals first conquered land, some took an extraordinary evolutionary U-turn and returned to the water. item.title: Breakthrough PTSD treatment achieves 68% remission rate in clinical trial
item.description: [Science & Research] Keyword: clinical trial — A newly FDA-cleared PTSD treatment uses personalized brain mapping and magnetic stimulation to target abnormal brain activity, with a clinical trial reporting a 52% reduction in symptoms and 68% remission. Researchers believe the technology could transform PTSD care and pave the way for more precise treatments for other mental health conditions.

item.title: Study highlights gender gap in AI media coverage in Spain
item.description: [Government Accountability] Keyword: FOIA — A media "glass ceiling" exists in news stories on artificial intelligence (AI) published in Spanish media in recent years: men are the main subjects in 41% of news reports, compared to just 5% featuring women. This is one of the findings of the report "InfoIA: Analysis of Information on Artificial Intelligence Published in Digital Media," conducted by the University Institute of Gender Studies at Universidad Carlos III de Madrid (UC3M).

item.title: AI agents can form political camps—and changing their conversation partners does little to soften their views
item.description: [AI & Automation] Keyword: AI agent — Give AI agents political positions, ask them to defend their views and persuade one another, and let them decide which contacts to keep. item.title: Millions take fish oil for brain health. A two-year study found no benefit
item.description: [Science & Research] Keyword: clinical trial — A surprising two-year clinical trial found that fish oil supplements successfully delivered omega-3s to the brain but failed to improve memory or protect against Alzheimer's-related brain shrinkage. Researchers suspect that getting these nutrients through a healthy diet may offer benefits that supplements alone cannot provide.

item.title: Europe's killer heat this summer claims 50,000 lives. Climate change blamed for two-thirds of deaths
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: climate change — Blistering record heat in Europe this summer helped kill more than 50,000 people, with nearly two-thirds of that death toll blamed on human-caused climate change, a new study found.
